text: The doctor was gentle and kind, and the service was excellent.
I have to say, it's really, really good!

I encountered a middle-aged female doctor who was heavy-handed, spoke somewhat impolitely, didn't explain the treatment plan well before or after, and often chatted with her assistant during patient consultations. This made me unsure if she was genuinely interested in providing treatment.

I went to the dentist on Sunday, and it turned out to be a part-time doctor who gave me medication that caused a rash – an allergic reaction. On Monday, I went to a new clinic to switch to different medication. When I arrived, the staff said the doctor only comes in once a week and they couldn't contact him. I asked if there were any other doctors at the clinic, but there wasn't a single one. Why open a clinic if there's no doctor available? A little while later, they called back and said, "Don't go to the doctor yet. The doctor has given you a trial run with different medications. Stop whichever one causes symptoms." Is this acceptable? I paid for the treatment myself, including medication and medical fees. I really regret wasting my money on this kind of service. The female doctor was also very heavy-handed and complained the whole time. This is paid treatment, not free!
